items.text: On May 15, Joe DiMaggio of the New York Yankees began his 56-game hitting streak.
items.question: Who in your family followed Joe DiMaggio's hitting streak, and how did you hear how he did each day?
items.source_quote: May 15 – Joe DiMaggio's 56-game hitting streak begins as the New York Yankee center fielder goes one for 4 against Chicago White Sox pitcher Eddie Smith.

items.text: Postage for a domestic letter was 3 cents an ounce.
items.question: Where were you living when a stamp for a letter cost three cents, and who did you write to?

items.text: Glenn Miller and His Orchestra's "Chattanooga Choo Choo" was a number-one song in the United States in 1941, according to The Billboard.
items.question: Where were you living when "Chattanooga Choo Choo" was on the radio, and who in your house danced to Glenn Miller?
source_quote: This is a list of number-one songs in the United States during the year 1941 according to The Billboard.
"Chattanooga Choo Choo" Glenn Miller and His Orchestra with Tex Beneke and the Four Modernaires

items.text: NBC Television began commercial operation on WNBT, and the first legal TV commercial, for Bulova watches, was shown before a baseball game between the Brooklyn Dodgers and the Philadelphia Phillies.
items.question: Do you remember the first television set you ever saw, and whose house or shop window was it in?
items.source_quote: NBC Television begins commercial operation on WNBT, on Channel 1. The world's first legal TV commercial, for Bulova watches, occurs at 2:29 PM over WNBT, before a baseball game between the Brooklyn Dodgers and Philadelphia Phillies.

items.text: On December 7, Pearl Harbor in Hawaii was attacked, and the United States was drawn into World War II.
items.question: Where were you on the day you heard about Pearl Harbor, and who told you?
items.source_quote: December 7 (07:48 Hawaiian Time; 12:48 EST; December 8 03:18 Japan Standard Time) – Attack on Pearl Harbor: The Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service stages a military strike on the United States Navy fleet at Pearl Harbor in the Territory of Hawaii, thus drawing the U.S. into World War II.
